blocks.text: DEMOLITION ACROSS EVERY TORONTO NEIGHBOURHOOD
★★★★★ 700+ Five-Star Reviews on Google
Demolition Services From Riverdale to North York — All of Toronto's Streets, One Precise Standard

c: Most demolition crews quote a job, show up, and discover the fence panel they were counting on removing is welded shut, or the only way out is a laneway their truck barely fits down. Live Junk Free scopes that stuff first. Semis in Riverdale, Leslieville, Roncesvalles and the Annex share walls and yards measured in feet, not metres — a garage or a deck coming down there means cutting things into carryable sections and threading them out a side passage, not swinging a wrecking ball. East York and North York’s postwar backyards give a lot more room to work with, so above ground pool demolition, shed teardowns and concrete removal there run closer to a standard job. And in the laneway-house pockets scattered through the west end, a structure sometimes has to come out through the same narrow lane the house itself was built around. Whatever the lot looks like, the 700+ five-star reviews behind Live Junk Free reflect one thing consistently: nothing left dented, scratched, or half-finished on a neighbour’s fence line.

blocks.text: WHY CHOOSE OUR DEMOLITION SERVICES
What Makes Toronto Demolition Different — and How We Handle It

items.title: Access gets solved before price does
text: A demolition quote that doesn’t account for how the debris actually leaves the property isn’t a real quote — it’s a guess that turns into a change order later. Live Junk Free walks the exit path first: gate width, laneway clearance, whether a fence panel comes off or the structure gets cut smaller instead. The number reflects reality, not an assumption.

items.title: One flat price, done — access included
text: Above ground pool, shed, deck, garage, fence, concrete pad — whatever’s coming down, teardown and haul-away sit inside a single figure agreed on site. A tight laneway doesn’t add a line to the invoice; it’s already factored into the number before the crew shows up.

items.title: Party-wall awareness on every shared-lot job
text: Row houses and semis mean structures often sit inches from a neighbour’s property line. Live Junk Free works with that in mind — vibration-conscious cutting, careful staging, nothing braced against a shared fence that isn’t yours to lean on.

items.title: Structures get cut down to fit the exit, not forced through it
text: A concrete pad, a wood deck and a steel-frame garage all fail differently if someone tries to drag them out whole. Each gets broken down with the technique its material actually calls for, sized to whatever gate, lane or gap is getting it off the property.

items.title: Booked today, gone today, more often than not
text: Call in the morning and there’s a real chance the structure’s down and hauled by evening. Trucks run seven days a week, 6AM to 11PM — useful in a city where a landscaper or contractor’s next visit is usually already on the calendar.

items.title: Independent pricing, not franchise pricing
text: The big national names build a royalty into every Toronto quote before the truck leaves the yard. Live Junk Free doesn’t carry that cost, and identical jobs typically land 30–50% lower here as a result.

blocks.text: DEMOLITION FAQ
Demolition Services in Toronto — Dense-City Questions, Precise Answers

items.q: What does demolition actually cost in Toronto?
a: One flat written figure per project, scoped free on site, covering labour, tear-out, loading, trucking and all disposal — with stairs, laneways, elevator time and congestion already inside it. Access never bills extra, and the approved number holds to the invoice.

items.q: We don't have backyard access, just a laneway. Is that a dealbreaker?
a: By treating the party wall as the project’s most important surface. Vibration-conscious methods, controlled plaster passes, nothing prying or hammering against the shared line, and containment sealed on our side — the neighbour’s home stays exactly as it was, which in this city is the whole job.

items.q: Will this damage our neighbour's fence or wall?
a: It’s a signature Toronto job for us. The old garage drops in sequence, the slab is addressed per your builder’s plan, debris exits through the lane the same day, and the cleared lot hands over matched to your suite drawings — with permit-likely work flagged at assessment and honoured.

items.q: Can you break up a concrete patio or walkway?
a: By the building’s book, before arrival. Certificates of insurance go to management at booking, freight elevators reserve ahead, corridors protect end to end, and quiet hours hold — renovation demo that concierges approve without a note.

items.q: Do you handle indoor hot tubs, or only backyard units?
a: Assumed nothing, verified everything. True plaster comes off in controlled passes, materials a century of renovations may have layered in get flagged and tested, and licensed abatement clears anything suspect before our demolition enters the zone.
